_about: Everything the tournament structure tunes with: the season length, the difficulty sawtooth, the rule twists, the location calendar, ranking points, rank titles, the placement reward table and the earned-gear generator. Numbers marked placeholder were set from the proposal (_reports/next-phase-proposal.md sections 2 and 3) and have not been tuned against real player scores (m2 measure is open).

warmup._about: Season 1's first events are a warm-up for a new player (Ed, 2026-10-21: Event 1 was too hard to pass). rivalScale[i] multiplies a rival's wave score in Season 1 event i+1; from the first event past the list it is 1, so the rivals meet the ordinary curve at Event 5. Target rival two-wave totals (best two of the rival's waves): Event 1 about 3 (two modest 2.5-point waves beat them nearly every time), then about 4.3, 5.8, 7.5, and Event 5 (about 9.7) is the ordinary curve. Real human pass rates are not measured: the play log (playLog below) is how they will be. forgiveEvents is how many of Season 1's first events forgive a heat's first wipeout: the wave scores what the rider earned before it (the normal parts, no exit bonus, scaled by ride length up to fullRideSeconds, at most cap), and the heat gives a fresh wave (one more wave and extraSeconds more clock).

playLog._about: The play log kept in the save so difficulty can be tuned from real play: the last maxWaves waves and the last maxHeats heats. Nothing is sent anywhere; Shift+L in the game saves the log as a JSON file.

curve._about: Per season s, g(s) = 1 - 1/(1 + (s-1)/approachK) runs from 0 toward 1 and never reaches it. A season starts at floor + (startLimit-floor)*g, climbs in a straight line over events 1..9 to peakFirst + (peakLimit-peakFirst)*g, and the Finale (event 10) adds the bump on top of the peak. Skill is the rivals' base skill (0..1); feet is the swell.

hazards._about: Hazard counts follow the old per-event ramp (sharks from event 3, reef from 2, closeouts from 4, loose boards from 5) for the first rampSeasons seasons, then stay at the level event rampSeasons*10 had.
hazards._lead: Where the first shark and the first loose board sit (metres down the wave from the drop-in) and the gap between hazards of one kind. The drop-in is z -16, speed about 10 m/s, so these give the player about 4 s to read the warning and steer; they were 30 and 36 (about 1.4 s) before the polish pass.

twists._about: Rule twists. A season from seasonTwistFrom on carries one season twist, picked in blocks of all six in a seeded order, active every event of the season. eventTwists are the fixed mid-season specials by event number (every season). At most maxActive are ever on at once (a season twist plus one event special).

priority-strict.label: Strict priority — interference zeros the wave

two-wave-set.label: Two-wave set — only two waves a heat, both count

short-heat.label: Short heat — 30 seconds on the clock

sideshore-wind.label: Side-shore wind — it shoves you down the face toward the trough

dry-reef.label: Dry reef — the rocks bite higher up the face

calendar._about: A season's ten stops, seeded by the season number. The home break is event 1 and the Finale. Premium stops are drawn from the locked-for-sale breaks, never in the first two events and never next to each other. Secondary stops use the other free breaks.

points._about: World Ranking Points by finish (1 = winner, 2 = runner-up, 4 = lost the semifinal, 8 = lost the quarterfinal, 16 = lost the round of 16). Points are never spent. The Finale pays finaleMultiplier. [placeholder]

ranks._about: Named steps with their point floors, then numbered steps forever: past the last name each step is growth times the one before (rounded to 10) and the title is the last name plus a Roman numeral (Legend II, III, ...). [placeholder]

rewards._about: Gear by placement, per season band. A finish gets its floor tier for sure and then rolls each chance, keeping the highest tier that hit. Finishes that yield nothing add one to the pity counter; with pityLimit of them in a row, the next finish gets a common. [placeholder]

gear._about: The earned-gear generator: pattern x palette x slot, per body, for the earned line only. Patterns are the basic painted ones (never solid, never an image print); there is no board shape other than the shortboard and no metallic finish here, those stay premium. When every table combination of a tier is owned, palettes are generated from a hue formula, so the supply never ends. Colours are fitted for the renderer by scripts/cloth-calibrate.mjs. Slots: board (both bodies), bottom (male board shorts, female bikini set), set (female rashguard set: rashguard and bottom in one pattern and colour pair), suit (female fullsuit). Men wear no tops and no suits.

kit.about: Chance that a male board-shorts or board win comes as a kit: the other piece in the same pattern and colours is granted with it (never forced; only if not owned yet). Women's gear is always a set: the bikini is top and bottom in one pattern, the rashguard set is rashguard and bottom in one pattern.
